newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gerrman air freight tries to avoid surcharges.
newsitem.headline: Gerrman air freight tries to avoid surcharges.

text.p: German forwarders said they have switched cargo away from airlines introducing a fuel surcharge to rival carriers holding back on introducing them.
U.S. airlines Delta Air Lines and American Airlines had benefitted in particular by late introduction of the standard 15 pfennig surcharge on rates, they said.

"Some shippers said they might transfer business to other carriers without surcharges. It has happened where it has been a delay," freight forwarders Danzas vice-president for airfreight in Germany, Volker Oesau told Reuters ON Friday.
"For example, Delta and American got more freight from us because the shippers wanted to save 15 pfennigs, especially as the U.S. airlines have lower rates anyway."

This had occurred over the first two weeks of November as the introduction by Lufthansa Cargo AG of a 15 pfennig fuel surcharge was gradually followed by all other airlines operating out of Germany," he added.

Oesau said forwarders with consolidation freight had been hit because freight accepted before the surcharge but flown after its introduction had to be charged to customers at the old price with the forwarder having to cover the surcharge himself.
"The problem with the surcharge is that it is coming so quickly and we have lost out in consolidation but there is nothing we can do about it," he said.
Lufthansa Germany sales manager, Florian Pfaff, defended the airline's worldwide four-day period of notice saying a surcharge could not be announced a month in advance.
"One week is of course short notice but others followed at even shorter notice," he added.
"It would be surprising if some (freight) switching had not happened. It is like with rates increases that there is a certain switching of freight," he told Reuters.
But this did not worry Lufthansa particularly since it was currently turning away freight.

Delta Germany cargo sales representative Manfred Schleiffer said: "It is too early to say if we have benefitted. There has perhaps been a slight increase but we normally have market growth at this time of the year anyway."
Delta joined the rest of the German market by adding a 15 pfennigs fuel surcharge Friday November 15.
